newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean says delivered money to mayor in crate.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean says delivered money to mayor in crate.

text.p: The chief accountant of South Korea's troubled Hanbo Group said on Monday he had delivered money in an apple crate to a close political associate of President Kim Young-sam.

The accountant, Kim Jong-kook, told a Seoul criminal court he had personally delivered 200 million won ($225,000) to Mayor Moon Jung-soo of Pusan, South Korea's second largest city, before elections in 1995.
"But I did not directly ask for favours concerning the company," Kim said.

The founder of Hanbo, Chung Tae-soo, had previously testified that he sent the funds through Kim Jong-kook to help finance the campaign during 1995 elections, when Moon was elected mayor, but denied bribing him.

Moon and seven serving or former lawmakers are on trial on charges of taking bribes from Chung, who is again on trial for corruption after being jailed in May for 15 years in a loans-for-kickbacks scandal.
The scandal landed in jail three other close associates of the president, including a former cabinet minister, along with bankers and businessmen.
Moon, a member of the president's inner circle that played a leading role in the 1992 presidential elections, has denied receiving the money.

State prosecutors accused Moon and the other politicians of taking kickbacks from the founder of Hanbo, whose steelmaking flagship collapsed in January under a mountain of debts, revealing a web of corruption. All other defendants have pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Opposition parties have alleged the president's second son, Kim Hyun-chul, pressured banks to keep loans flowing to Hanbo Steel, but the prosecution has cleared him of involvement in the loan scandal.
But the younger Kim was arrested in May on charges of tax evasion and bribery in separate scandals, dealing a blow to President Kim's already tarnished administration.
Kim Hyun-chul, who is also on trial, has denied receiving money in return for business favours.
